scope: Stable in-session editing targets when inner pages are appended after deletion, replenished after authored-page deletion, or extended by template application.

findings.before: Additional inner pages were assigned page_<current length>. Deletion retained the IDs of surviving pages, so a later append could duplicate a surviving ID. The blank replacement after deleting from a fully authored book had the same problem. Tail deletion followed by addition also revived a removed ID within the same editing session, allowing that ID to denote a different target.
evidence: A 24-inner-page book with pages 1-2 removed then two pages added had 25 pages but only 23 distinct IDs.
Deleting an authored page when no blank partner existed added a blank replacement whose ID was already present.
Deleting and recreating the final spread reused removed target IDs under the same editSessionIdentity.
Template extension after a middle deletion reproduced the same ID collision.
A repeated remove/add fixture reused a target ID on its first cycle.
findings.change: Generate a UUID-backed local ID only for newly appended inner pages. Share that creation helper between padding/addition, template extension and blank replacement. Leave all retained page IDs, initial cover/page creation and session identity unchanged.

initial_fixture_load.classification: The first helper used a contextually inferred async return cascade, which inferred FutureOr<AlbumEditorViewModel> and failed compilation. Corrected the helper by using a local variable; no production issue was inferred from this fixture error.

controlled_baseline.classification: Intentional before-fix reproductions of five page-identity cases.

related_tests.command: nice -n 10 flutter test --no-test-assets --no-pub --concurrency=1 --reporter expanded test/unit/album_editor_page_identity_test.dart test/unit/album_editor_view_model_test.dart test/unit/album_page_policy_test.dart --name 'page identity|printable editor page policy|resetForCreate|addPage and removeLastPage|new selections|template minimum|undo and redo'
coverage: Five new identity regressions including 30 repeated deletion/addition cycles.
Existing minimum/maximum 20-80 page policy, even/odd legacy padding and deletion, template addition/cap rejection, retained authored/background content, reset and undo/redo behavior.

static_analysis.post_test_cleanup: Removed only an unnecessary material.dart import from the new test after analysis; final analysis confirms symbol resolution. Production behavior and all test bodies were unchanged after the passing run; the suite was not redundantly rerun.

verification.scoped_git_diff_check: passed; exact source replacement against the pre-run snapshot also checked

resources.handling: Checked known active Flutter test/build/run/compiler and render/export processes before starting. Ran one agent-owned test process at a time with concurrency=1 and nice 10. Static analysis ran after the test process completed, also with nice 10. Used no-test-assets for these local model/policy fixtures and did not regenerate asset bundles or delete caches.

verification.external_effects: No app build, running app/device, preview server, deployment, production database operation, purchase or customer album mutation.

checked: All three live append paths use the helper; initialization paths still use their existing initial IDs.
Retained page IDs, order, pageIndex, backgrounds and photo/layer objects are preserved by the controlled retention cases.
New IDs are allocated only during explicit model additions; no work is added to scrolling, cover rendering, image decoding or list building.
The existing UUID dependency is reused. There is no extra cache, historical ID set, subscriber, timer, queue or worker.
The page-ID consumers inspected use opaque identity comparisons; no numeric parsing of page IDs was found in the album feature.
The full album serializer continues using page index/isCover/background/layers and was not edited; existing saved content, product metadata and layer photo references are untouched.
The previous decoration target guard and point-shop access code remain byte-identical to their pre-run snapshots.
No other task work or existing dirty workspace change was reset, overwritten or removed.

next_candidates: Inspect pending frame/phrase application at their editor caller boundaries, using the latest target/page policy code and a concrete delayed-completion regression before changing it.

Review whether an already-loaded legacy document can contain duplicate local targets through a different path; do not rename saved/retained IDs without a separate controlled case and preservation plan.
Resume main/store/reader hidden/resume and stale-owner checks after reviewing newer verification records; preserve completed request sharing, discovery sort/badge rules and catalog ownership.

limits: No physical-device FPS, frame time, peak application/native memory or heap leak profile was measured. New IDs are small local metadata allocated on explicit addition, not a measured memory/performance result.

UUID v4 generation uses the existing dependency and provides practical unique identity; the regression checks validate the controlled sequences rather than mathematically proving every possible random ID.
This fix prevents new duplicate/revived IDs on the three affected append paths. It does not migrate or rename already retained/saved pages, and no production/customer data was inspected or rewritten.
